articles.title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI judges, models that grade another system's output against a rubric, extend clinical review to the scale at which clinical AI writes. When teams use judge assessments to select a prompt or train a model, the judge becomes part of the intervention. Selection can then favor errors the judge overlooks. We describe what a judge's report must contain and the independent clinical test each judge-driven change needs.

articles.title: Beyond Curiosity: Habit and Organizational Learning Capability as Predictors of Shadow AI
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.16931v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generative AI has entered the workplace faster than organizations can govern it. Employees may use AI tools their employer has not sanctioned and conceal that use, but the psychology of this behavior remains poorly understood. We compare an exploratory-disposition account with one centered on reported use and habit. articles.title: Curating Safe Spaces for Emotion Disclosure during Illness Recovery on Video-Sharing Platforms
articles.summary: arXiv:2502.20658v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The advent of video-sharing platforms has transformed self-expression, transcending entertainment to encompass sensitive disclosures and emotional revelations. In this submission, we discuss our study on emotional disclosure by individuals with Schizophrenia through YouTube vlogs and its implications for designing safe online spaces.

articles.title: Toward Operationalizing Rasmussen in Evolving Software Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2602.05483v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Rasmussen's qualitative drift model explains how successive, locally successful adaptations under efficiency pressures can move a system toward unacceptable operation. Brooker and Hochstein applied this perspective conceptually to software operations without specifying a quantitative procedure for observing drift. We take a step in this direction and propose a runtime observer that quantitatively operationalizes the model's observable part for evolving software.
